plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Probability, Years 5 and 6 (VC2M5P02, VC2M6P02): list the outcomes of chance activities, with and without equally likely outcomes, and describe their likelihood as fractions
plan.shape: compare-two-models: an equal spinner beside an unequal one, because counting equal parts instead of colours is the new idea
plan.criticalFeature: count the equally likely parts, not the colours
decisionPoints: the choice check: which event has a probability of 1/2?
the hinge: P(red) on an unequal spinner
plan.anchor: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes

manipulatives: A dice and a coin for every pair (optional, for checking outcomes)
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
A chance line: impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely, certain

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. List outcomes, write probabilities from spinners, sport and game problems, and a mistake to fix.
resources.title: Outcomes and Chance
resources.subtitle: Chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes.

example.prompt: What are the outcomes of spinning a spinner with 4 equal parts: red, blue, red, green?
steps: Read each part: red, blue, red, green.
The different results are red, blue and green.
example.answer: red, blue, green (red is 2 of 4 parts)

items.prompt: List every outcome, then count them.
rows: Spin a red, blue, green spinner
Pick a day of the week
answers: Spin a red, blue, green spinner
Pick a day of the week

example.prompt: What is P(blue) on a spinner with 5 equal parts, 2 of them blue?
A team of 10 picks a captain at random. 4 players are Year 5. What is the chance the captain is in Year 5?
steps: All the equally likely outcomes: 10 players.
The ones we want: 4 Year 5 players.

items.prompt: A netball team of 7 picks a captain at random. 3 players are in Year 6. What is the probability the captain is in Year 6?
A footy club raffle sells 50 tickets. Sam buys 5. What is his chance of winning? Simplify it.
Kai worked out P(red) for this spinner. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: Red takes 2 of the 4 equal parts, so P(red) = 2/4 = 1/2. Count parts, not colours.

items.explain: Tossing heads is 1/2; rolling a 5 is only 1/6.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Two coins, number cards and designing a spinner, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Coins, Cards and Spinners
resources.subtitle: List every outcome before you count.

example.prompt: List the outcomes of tossing two coins.

items.prompt: Two coins are tossed. What is the probability of two heads?
What is the probability of one head and one tail? Explain.
items.answer: 2/4 = 1/2: HT and TH are both one head and one tail.

example.prompt: Cards 1 to 10. What is P(a number less than 4)?

items.prompt: Cards numbered 1 to 10 are shuffled and one is picked.
Design a spinner with 8 equal parts where P(blue) = 3/8, P(red) = 1/4 and the rest is green. Draw it and write P(green).
items.answer: 3 blue parts, 2 red parts (1/4 = 2/8), 3 green parts. P(green) = 3/8.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: spinners to count part by part, a fraction frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Chance: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Count the parts. Write ___ out of ___.

items.hint: Count every part first. Then count blue.

items.prompt: Roll a dice. P(3) = ___ out of ___
Roll a dice. P(1 or 2) = ___ out of ___

slides.notes: Session 1 of our probability week: today we list outcomes and write chance as a fraction.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and a dice and a coin per pair if you have them. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Read the graph
prompts: How many more chose grapes than banana?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's statistics.
ASK: How many more students chose grapes than banana?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 6
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> lay a ruler across each column top and read the scale. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Grapes 11, banana 5, so 6 more chose grapes. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 11, the grapes value.
Fix: ask what 'how many more' means, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Review of Week 3 statistics (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: Which display suits rainfall each month?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a line graph
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> ask: categories, a few numbers, or change over time? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: A line graph, because the rainfall changes over time. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing a column graph.
Fix: ask whether the rainfall changes over time, and they choose again.

slides.title: Read a point
prompts: What are the coordinates of K?

beats: ASK: What are the coordinates of K?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (3, 6)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> slide across, then up, on the big grid. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 3, 6: across 3, then up 6. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (6, 3).
Fix: say the anchor, across first, and they rewrite it.

beats: SAY: Now for our seven times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 7 times 6?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 42
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 5 sevens is 35, then one more 7. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 42. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 36 or 48.
Fix: use 5 sevens is 35, plus one more 7, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 7 times 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 56
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 7 sevens is 49, then one more 7. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 56. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 54.
Fix: count on one more 7 from 7 times 7, 49, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many sevens make 63?
ASK: What is 63 divided by 7?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in sevens from 56. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 9. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 8.
Fix: check: 8 sevens is 56, one more is 63, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to describe the chance of an outcome and write it as a fraction.
successCriteria: I can list all the possible outcomes of a chance event.
I can write the probability of an outcome as a fraction.
I can explain whether the outcomes are equally likely.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week is all about chance.
Today we learn to say exactly how likely something is, as a fraction.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 listing outcomes is reachable for everyone; SC2 writing the probability is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 equally likely is the stretch.

slides.title: How likely is it?
slides.prompt: Roll a normal dice. Where does 'rolling a 7' go?

beats: POINT to each word on the chance line.
SAY: Some of you may know these chance words, from impossible to certain.
ASK: If you roll a normal dice,
where on the line does 'rolling a 7' go?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: impossible
SCAN boards for impossible.
80%+ -> ask: where does 'rolling a number from 1 to 6' go?
Less -> hold up a dice and count its faces together. Re-ask.
SAY: Rolling a 7 is impossible, because no face has a 7.
Today we go further than words: we'll say chance with a fraction.
trap: saying unlikely.
Fix: count the faces on a real dice, and they place it again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: chance words before chance numbers. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: One possible result of a chance event.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is outcome. Say it with me: out-come.
SAY: An outcome is one possible result.
When you roll a dice, there are six outcomes, one for each face.
ASK: How many outcomes are there when you toss a coin?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2
trap: saying 1 outcome for a coin.
Fix: name them together, heads and tails, and they count again.
notes.prep: Outcome is the word the anchor depends on.

slides.title: List outcomes, write the chance
steps: List the outcomes: red, blue, green, yellow.
The 4 parts are equal, so each is equally likely.

beats: POINT to each part.
SAY: First I list the outcomes: red, blue, green and yellow.
The four parts are the same size, so each is equally likely.
MODEL writing P(red) = 1/4.
SAY: Red is one part out of four equal parts,
so the probability of red is one quarter. We write it as P of red.
ASK: What is the probability of landing on red or blue?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/4. ACCEPT: 1/2
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Two parts out of four, which is two quarters, or one half.
trap: writing 2/2.
Fix: count all the parts as the bottom number, and they rewrite it.
notes.help: Write: ___ parts we want out of ___ parts.
notes.prep: The anchor: the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: When parts are not equal
steps: Red covers half the spinner: 2 of 4 equal parts.
Red and blue are not equally likely.

beats: POINT to the spinner.
SAY: This spinner has three colours, but the parts are not the same size.
MODEL splitting red into two equal parts.
SAY: Red covers half, so I split it into two quarters.
Now there are 4 equal parts, and red has 2 of them.
ASK: So what is the probability of green?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1/4
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's one quarter, not one third.
We count equal parts, not colours.
trap: writing 1/3 because there are 3 colours.
Fix: split the spinner into equal parts, and they count again.
notes.stretch: Change one colour so all three are equally likely.
notes.help: Draw lines to split the spinner into equal parts.
notes.prep: The critical feature: count equal parts, not colours. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Which has a probability of 1/2?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: thinks any single outcome is 50/50: it happens or it doesn't

options.text: picking red from 1 red and 2 blue counters
options.misconception: counts colours, not counters: 1 of 2 colours

beats: SAY: Think about all the equally likely outcomes for each one.
ASK: Which event has a probability of one half?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What is the chance for C?
Less -> list the outcomes for each on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B: heads is 1 of 2 outcomes.
A is 1 out of 6,
and C is 1 out of 3, because there are 3 counters.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: count the faces of a dice together, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A means 'it happens or not' thinking; C means colours were counted, not counters.

slides.title: What is the probability?
slides.ask: What is the probability? Write a fraction.
slides.pivot: count all the equal parts, then the ones we want
slides.followUp: cold call one board: What did you count for the bottom number?

items.text: A bag has 2 red, 3 blue and 5 green counters. P(blue)?
Roll a dice. P(an even number)?
items.say: Three faces are even, 2, 4 and 6, so 3/6 or 1/2.

say: Write each probability as a fraction on your board.
trap: putting the wrong number on the bottom.
Fix: ask how many outcomes there are altogether, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write each answer as a decimal too.
notes.help: Write 'we want' and 'altogether' before the fraction.
notes.prep: Guided practice: dice, equal and unequal spinners, counters, then two outcomes we want. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Look carefully at the size of each part.
ASK: What is the probability of red?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/4. ACCEPT: 1/2
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> draw the line that splits red into two quarters. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Red is half the spinner, 2 of 4 equal parts,
so P of red is a half. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 1/3.
Fix: split red into equal parts, and they count again.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone who wrote 1/3 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: List outcomes and write probabilities on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What did you count for the bottom number?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: counting colours instead of equal parts.
Fix: split the spinner into equal parts, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: two coins, number cards and designing a spinner.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: spinners to count part by part and a fraction frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: outcomes, probabilities, sport problems and a mistake. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: What is the probability of picking a yellow counter?

visual.text: A bag holds 4 red, 1 blue and 3 yellow counters.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the probability of picking a yellow counter?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/8
RECORD who writes 1/3 or 3/5.
They start tomorrow's experiment with the teacher.
trap: writing 1/3, from 3 colours.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new context with unequal numbers of each colour.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how to work out a probability.

notes.answer: open - listen for the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can write a probability as a fraction?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 1/3 on the board matters most.
ASK: How do you work out a probability?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow we run real experiments.
